output.myth: Kael the Netter cast for fallen stars every night and never once hauled one up. One night the net came back heavy and wet, and in it was a gull, the first she had ever caught. Kael's hands shook, because the mesh had her by the wing and she would not stop beating. He thought of Hesk at the pole, who keeps count of every thing that is taken, and he thought of the fallen star still falling somewhere past the Lamp Road. So he loosed the knot, one thread at a time, and let her go. Tavo took her up at once, laughing, and she went off over the Windward Reach with a square of net still tangled in her wing. She is up there now. Look for her when the wind is right: she goes back and forth between the lamps, and the knot-mark shows pale on her wing. Kael still casts. He comes home, empty-handed.
output.verse:
Net-knot on her wing
she tacks back and forth in wind
Kael still casts for stars

problems: The blind guess (a bird in flight with a long neck) matches the gist of a gull in flight. The heron/crane reading comes from the tall, narrow body, not from the wing shape.
Right orientation: head star 84380 sits at the top (about 340,183), tail star 84379 at the bottom (about 349,399). The figure is upright.

Star placement is mostly right: breast 84573 sits at the wing junction (about 333,250), right wingtip 83207 at (401,285), left wingtip 89935 at (85,319), and the left trailing edge 87933 and feather tip 86974 lie along the left wing.
The net-mark 88745 at about (141,293) is a small ring but sits on the edge of the outline, not clearly inside the left wing.
The body is a thin vertical stick with no round head, so the gull's head does not read as a head.
The tail fork is not visible. Only a single tail point at 84379 is drawn.
The right wing is a tiny stub compared with the long left wing, so the bird looks lopsided.
The gold skeleton lines dominate; the blue contour is hairline-thin and does not read as a filled silhouette.
Labels overlap lines and stars, and the 'tail tip' and 'head' labels are cut off at the frame edge.
judge.advice: Keep the drawing; it passes. Optional improvements: (1) Draw a rounded head around 84380 at the top, about 8-10px across, so the head reads as a head. (2) Add a forked tail below 84573 that splits around 84379 at the bottom, so the tail reads as forked. (3) Enlarge the right wing so its tip 83207 at (401,285) balances the left wing reaching 89935 at (85,319). (4) Move the net-mark 88745 at (141,293) inside the left wing outline, between the body and the trailing edge. (5) Thicken the blue contour so it reads as a silhouette rather than a hairline. (6) Shorten the labels so they stay inside the frame.

guess: A bird in flight, possibly a heron or crane with a long neck
